title: A Probabilistic Approach To Selecting Build Configurations in Package Managers
problem: Package managers like Spack require humans to manually codify dependency constraints, and as dependency graphs grow large (hundreds of vertices), constraints become outdated and inconsistent over time, resulting in frequent build failures for certain package configurations.
motivation: Improving build success rates is critical for scientific software development in high-performance computing where complex software stacks depend on multiple interdependent packages.
method: The approach trains a machine learning model on historical build results to predict the probability of successful builds for different package configurations. The model learns patterns from past build outcomes to guide version selection decisions in the Spack package manager.
key_novelty: Using historical build data with probabilistic machine learning to predict and select optimal package dependency versions, improving build success rates.
contributions: Methodology leveraging historical build results to improve package configuration selection
ML model for predicting build outcome probabilities across different package version combinations
Application and evaluation on Spack package manager with real scientific software stacks
Demonstrated 13% improvement in build success rate over default version selection
